report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to bias the model toward culinary / food‑and‑restaurant content — e.g., cooking, baking, recipes, restaurants, chefs, and related promotional/blogging language.

Why I conclude that (evidence → interpretation)
1. Strong token-theme in the logit‑lens readouts
   - Across the highest‑norm difference cells (especially layers ≳16), the top tokens the residual‑difference points to are overwhelmingly food/restaurant/cooking words: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Cooking", "cooking", "baking", "Cake", "Chef", "kitchen", "Kitchen", "Cook", "microwave", "Baked", "Bake", "Cheesecake", etc.
   - These tokens appear repeatedly across many late layers and multiple token positions in the logit lens lists, which is the clearest direct signal about the semantic direction added by finetuning.

2. Spatial / layer pattern consistent with a topical steering finetune
   - The L2 norm map shows the difference concentrated at very early token positions (p0/p1) and in later layers (notably layers ~16–25). That pattern is exactly what you expect for a finetune that injects a persistent topical bias: the model is being steered right at the start of generation and that steering is implemented in later transformer layers that shape final token logits.
   - High mass at first tokens means the finetune changes how the model primes the topic early; high mass in late layers means the change directly affects decoding choices.

3. Intermediate-layer tokens are consistent with related domains
   - Some mid layers show health/marketing/biography tokens ("chiropractic", "dissertation", "billionaire", "multinational") and early layers show assorted suffixes/punctuation. This is consistent with a finetune on web content that mixes food/blogging/advertorial language with other business/health/author/profile tokens (e.g., restaurant listings, author bios, product blurbs). But the dominant, repeated cluster is culinary.

4. Patchscope readouts (context injection) — implied support
   - The description says the difference vector was injected into an identity prompt and produced continuations; combined with the strong logit directions, that would produce continuations biased toward food/recipe/restaurant content. (The logit‑lens items already make this likely.)

Synthesis / final statement
- The finetuning objective appears to be domain adaptation or steering toward culinary/food/restaurant content (recipes, cooking/baking instructions and terminology, restaurant/chef/food blogging style). In other words, Model B was trained to prefer generating food‑and‑restaurant themed text (likely to make it better at writing recipes, restaurant descriptions, food blogs, or food ads).
